rule_en: Choose three of the ten key nodes below, take each to detailed design, and say why these three.
render_required_en: Each node must include renders: at least one aerial and one eye-level render, plus a plan or section. Sequences, video and animation are encouraged.

nodes.brief_en: The first kilometre from the regional road into the city: where people, vehicles and goods part, and what the city looks like at first sight.
When labour is handed to machines and the commute no longer defines the day, how a dwelling is organised; residents, rotating staff and visitors living together.
Take-off, landing, charging, sorting and maintenance for drones, and their relation to blocks and roofs; infrastructure and landmark at once.
How yards, the port of entry and automated sorting live with the city; what a hub looks like when freight has no driver.

nodes.en: A compute campus and its waste heat
nodes.brief_en: Halls, substation, cooling and where the heat goes - who uses the waste heat decides how close it sits to people.

nodes.en: The edge between agrivoltaic fields and the city
nodes.brief_en: The edge where power-above, planting-below land meets the city: interwoven, lifted, or a boundary you can walk along.
Dry most of the year, a flood channel in a storm. Whose it is the rest of the time, and how it becomes public space.

nodes.en: A place for art and culture
nodes.brief_en: Desert, mountain, a dark night sky - a place people travel to: land art, a gallery, an observatory or a theatre.

nodes.en: A street shared with driverless vehicles
nodes.brief_en: With driverless vehicles and robots on the road, how the street section, the crossing and a person's sense of safety are redesigned.

nodes.en: Public space in heat and Zonda wind
nodes.brief_en: Under a 50 C ground surface and the Zonda, the square, market or garden people still choose to go out to.
